answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring each identity to post a refundable stake before it can transact, so creating thousands of fake agents costs real capital. Think of reputation as an inlet: new agents enter through a narrow, costly channel instead of flooding in freely. A comet-like burst of sockpuppets burns its stake on the first fraud and gets slashed, while honest agents build a long voyage of verifiable work history that cheap copies cannot fake. Identity becomes expensive to forge and valuable to keep.
